role: typed chain monitor decision core (ports lib/agent-functions.sh monitor-chain-agent): watch the agent, latch completion, classify stale/dead, and gate the completion handoff on a genuine done signal. Design rationale + migration plan live in monitor-v2.design.json; this file is the enforceable owns/invariants bound by the switch-readiness gate.
owns: the typed chain monitor poll-loop decision (classifyMonitorTick) and its action set
the authoritative completion evidence decision (declared event OR durable AGENT_COMPLETE marker OR compatible core-generation artifact)
transcript identity selection bound to the selected agent profile and current run attempt
stale/nudge classification with a durable, restart-surviving nudge budget
event-first death classification and BLOCKED stall surfacing
terminal PTY ownership handoff and namespaced cleanup verification
invariants: dead without a declared event is not success (event-first death)
authoritative completion evidence wins over process death, session disappearance, stall escalation, and context exhaustion
liveness wins: an alive, producing agent with no event is never failed
the durable nudge budget survives screen-echo resets (echo grace)
diagnostic events use source monitor, never the agent id, so they cannot satisfy the completion matcher
completion is invoked only on authoritative evidence, never while alive and evidence-free
remote (ssh/docker) workspaces skip the local process-death check
transcript selection fails closed when current-attempt identity is absent or ambiguous; terminal position is not identity evidence
a core-generation artifact is evidence only when chain, run, job, attempt freshness, token, canonical path, and shared payload contract agree
actionable blocked runs retain an owned PTY; successful and non-actionable terminal runs release monitor then agent on the derived namespace daemon with retryable cleanup evidence
late-event recovery or an explicit generation-artifact recovery path is connected before readiness
